thread.title: As iPhone Sales Stall, This Will Drive Apple Growth

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: As iPhone Sales Stall, This Will Drive Apple Growth
text:
The iPhone is no longer a growth engine for Apple ( AAPL ), but the company has other businesses to offset the maturing smartphone business, investment bank Morgan Stanley said Thursday.
X "As Apple's prospects for generating outsized iPhone growth fade as the handset market matures, some investors fear Apple's best days are behind it," Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty said in a report. "We disagree and see increasing value in the Apple platform, particularly through Services monetization."
Huberty predicts that services will account for about 60% of Apple's revenue growth over the next five years. Services include the App Store, iTunes, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, AppleCare and other offerings.
The company's Other Products business segment will make up about 30% of Apple's growth during the next five years, she said. The Other Products segment includes Apple Watch, Apple TV, HomePod, AirPods, Beats headphones, and miscellaneous devices and accessories.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Together, Services and Other Products "will drive almost all of Apple's growth over the next five years," she said.
By contrast, over the last five years, the vast majority (86%) of Apple's revenue growth was driven by iPhone sales, Huberty said. Apple's iPhone sales recently have been affected by market saturation and lengthening replacement cycles.
Huberty predicts that Apple's revenue growth will slow to a 6% compound annual growth rate over the next five years, vs. 8% for the last five years. But the growth rate for earnings per share is seen accelerating to a 16% compound annual growth rate over the next five years, vs. 8% for the previous five years, thanks to higher-margin services and increased share repurchases.
Huberty reiterated her overweight rating on Apple stock with a price target of 203.
Apple shares lost 1.4% to close at 168.85 on the stock market today . Since hitting an all-time high of 183.50 on March 13, Apple stock has fallen in seven of the last eight trading sessions. On Wednesday, Apple closed below its 50-day moving average line, a negative technical trading sign.
